" in " + esc(m.mod.split("/").pop()) + "" : SCOPE ? " in " + esc(SCOPE) + "" : "") + ", " + m.edges.length + " relationship(s). Each edge is labelled with the FIELD it goes " + "through; * is a list. Click a box to open its definition." + (m.ctxShown ? " " + m.ctxShown + " faded box(es) sit OUTSIDE this filter and are drawn because " + "something here links to them — a cut edge is the one most worth seeing." : "") + (m.ctxHidden ? " " + m.ctxHidden + " further neighbour(s) not drawn." : "") + /* Both endpoints ARE drawn, so an unreported suppression reads as "these two are unrelated" -- a false statement the picture makes silently. */ (m.ctxEdges ? " " + m.ctxEdges + " relationship(s) BETWEEN two faded boxes are not drawn, because " + "the picture is about this filter rather than about its surroundings — counted here so a missing " + "line is never mistaken for a missing relationship." : "") + /* Said rather than left to be noticed: a wrapped layer looks like two layers to a reader who was not told, and the alternative the panel used to take was to shrink the whole picture without saying so. */ (wrapped ? " " + wrapped + " row(s) wrapped to keep the boxes at full size." : "") + (crowded ? " " + crowded + " label(s) had nowhere clear to sit and overlap a box — hover the edge's boxes to read the field." : ""); key.innerHTML = 'generalisation (extends)' + 'field reference — in the source' + 'id reference — DECLARED with @ref, because a string id is invisible to a syntactic reader'; } function render() { var f = filterState(); var rows = G.decls.filter(function (d) { return matchesFilter(d, f.q, f.k, f.m); }); $("items").innerHTML = rows.slice(0, 400).map(function (d) { return ' | ' + '' + esc(d.name) + "" + (d.kind === "undetermined" ? 'undetermined' : '' + esc(d.kind) + "") + (kindsOf(d).length ? '' + esc(kindsOf(d).map(function (r) { return r.id; }).join(", ")) + "" : "") + '' + esc(d.module.split("/").pop()) + " | "; }).join("") || ' | Nothing matches. | '; $("counts").textContent = ""; var scoped = G.decls.filter(inScope); var mods = G.modules.filter(function (m) { return !SCOPE || m.instance === SCOPE; }); /* Edges are scoped too. Reporting the graph-wide 512 on a page showing 9 declarations says there are 512 edges among those 9, which is a claim the page does not support. An edge COUNTS here when it leaves a declaration this page shows — edges INTO the subject from elsewhere are real and are still followable from the detail panel, they are just not this subject's own outgoing structure. */ var edgeCount = SCOPE ? G.edges.filter(function (e) { var f = G.declIndex[e.from]; return f && inScope(f); }).length : G.edges.length; $("counts").innerHTML = (SCOPE ? "" + SCOPE + " · " : "") + "" + rows.length + " of " + scoped.length + " declarations · " + mods.length + " modules · " + edgeCount + " edges · " + scoped.filter(function (d) { return d.kind === "undetermined"; }).length + " undetermined"; var srcs = (G.sources || []).filter(nkInScope).length; if (srcs) $("counts").innerHTML += " · " + srcs + " source descriptor" + (srcs === 1 ? "" : "s"); /* A scope with descriptors and no modules has no declarations to browse: the declaration panels are hidden rather than shown empty. */ var onlySources = srcs > 0 && mods.length === 0; ["overview", "kinds"].forEach(function (id) { $(id).hidden = onlySources; }); /* style, not the hidden attribute: .sc-main sets display: grid, which outranks the attribute's display: none. */ document.querySelector(".sc-page .sc-main").style.display = onlySources ? "none" : ""; renderKinds(); renderSources(); } function select(id) { var d = byId(id); if (!d) return; SEL = id; if (location.hash.slice(1) !== encodeURIComponent(id)) { try { history.replaceState(null, "", "#" + encodeURIComponent(id)); } catch (e) { /* opened from a file */ } } render(); detail(d); var dt = $("detail"); if (dt && (window.innerWidth window.innerHeight / 2)) { try { dt.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth", block: "start" }); } catch (e) { dt.scrollIntoView(); } dt.focus(); } } fetch(DATA_HREF).then(function (r) { if (!r.ok) throw new Error(String(r.status)); return r.json(); }).then(function (data) { G = data; G.declIndex = {}; G.decls.forEach(function (d) { G.declIndex[d.id] = d; }); // A declaration names its module; the module names its instance. Joined // here once rather than at each filter, so the scope test stays O(1). var instOf = {}; G.modules.forEach(function (m) { instOf[m.module] = m.instance; }); G.decls.forEach(function (d) { d.instance = instOf[d.module]; }); G.nkByDecl = {}; (G.nodeKinds || []).forEach(function (r) { if (r.decl) (G.nkByDecl[r.decl] = G.nkByDecl[r.decl] || []).push(r); }); var kinds = [...new Set(G.decls.map(function (d) { return d.kind; }))].sort(); kinds.forEach(function (k) { var o = document.createElement("option"); o.value = k; o.textContent = k; $("kind").appendChild(o); }); var nko = document.createElement("option"); nko.value = "@nk"; nko.textContent = "defines a node kind or family"; $("kind").appendChild(nko); $("nk-rows").addEventListener("click", function (e) { var b = e.target.closest("button[data-sel]"); if (!b) return; select(b.getAttribute("data-sel")); $("detail").scrollIntoView({ block: "start" }); }); var withDecls = {}; G.decls.forEach(function (d) { withDecls[d.module] = true; }); /* Labelled with the instance, because four of them declare a schemas graph and module names repeat across them — two entries both reading "types" are indistinguishable in the list even though their values differ. */ var nameCount = {}; G.modules.forEach(function (m) { nameCount[m.name] = (nameCount[m.name] || 0) + 1; }); G.modules.forEach(function (m) { if (!withDecls[m.module]) return; if (SCOPE && m.instance !== SCOPE) return; var o = document.createElement("option"); o.value = m.module; o.textContent = nameCount[m.name] > 1 ? m.instance + " / " + m.name : m.name; $("mod").appendChild(o); }); /* Redrawn only when the panel is OPEN; a closed one costs nothing, and the toggle handler below draws it on first open. */ function redrawIfOpen() { if ($("overview").open) diagram(); } /* Search is debounced and the two selects are not: a select fires once per choice, while typing fires per keystroke and the layout is the expensive part -- the same trade the resize handler below makes, at the same 150ms. The LIST stays undebounced either way, so typing still feels immediate; only the picture waits. */ var flt; $("q").addEventListener("input", function () { render(); clearTimeout(flt); flt = setTimeout(redrawIfOpen, 150); }); /* The diagram narrows with EVERY filter, not just the module one. A 754-declaration instance is over DIA_MAX and refuses to draw, so before this the only way to get a picture was to know which module to pick; a search that narrows the set under the limit now earns one too. */ $("kind").addEventListener("change", function () { render(); redrawIfOpen(); }); $("mod").addEventListener("change", function () { render(); redrawIfOpen(); }); $("items").addEventListener("click", function (e) { var b = e.target.closest("button[data-id]"); if (b) select(b.getAttribute("data-id")); }); /* A node navigates; it does not move. In declaration mode it selects, in module mode it filters the list to that module — the overview hands you off to the panel that answers the local question. */ $("ov-svg").addEventListener("click", function (e) { var c = e.target.closest("[data-ov]"); if (!c) return; var id = c.getAttribute("data-ov"); if (byId(id)) { select(id); return; } $("mod").value = id; render(); $("list").scrollIntoView({ block: "start" }); }); $("overview").addEventListener("toggle", function () { /* Drawn on first open rather than at load: a reader who never opens the panel should not pay for a layout over 812 declarations. */ if ($("overview").open && !$("ov-svg").childNodes.length) diagram(); }); /* The width budget is the panel's own width, so a resize changes how many boxes fit a row. Without this the layout keeps the width it was built at and the reader is back to a shrunk picture -- the defect the budget exists to remove. Debounced, because a drag fires this continuously and the layout is the expensive part. */ var rsz; window.addEventListener("resize", function () { if (!$("overview").open || !$("ov-svg").childNodes.length) return; clearTimeout(rsz); rsz = setTimeout(diagram, 150); }); $("detail").addEventListener("click", function (e) { var a = e.target.closest('a[href^="#"]'); if (a) { e.preventDefault(); select(decodeURIComponent(a.getAttribute("href").slice(1))); } }); render(); if (location.hash.length > 1) select(decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1))); }).catch(function (e) { $("counts").textContent = "could not load the projection: " + e.message; $("detail").innerHTML = 'The projection at ' + esc(DATA_HREF) + ' could not be read. ' + "That is not an empty graph \u2014 it is a graph that could not be loaded, and the page says so rather than showing nothing. "; });

447.title: Glossary swimlane-glossary
447.content: Derived: every term this instance's swimlanes define — the role's title and description, the lane names that bind it, and whether the term has been retired. Sub-graph cat-harness/glossary, 61 entries. This is an index, not the documentation. It says what exists and what each artefact declares about itself. What a process is for, when you would be in it, and what it is not, is authored beside it and reuses these entries rather than restating them — see the auto-docs skill. Filter this table | Artefact | What it declares about itself | . | Activity logglossary-ledger.json | The agent activity log. A MECHANICAL role and an actedUpon one: it is written to at task start and task end, and emptied by an actor — one entry, all of them, or on a periodic sweep — and it decides nothing. Modelled on work-plan and corpus, the two existing stores that are acted upon rather than acting. Its entries are held in the instance's unpublished store and never reach a published graph; the activity-log skill names the location, which is deliberately not repeated here because a role description IS published.notation role/logfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Actorbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation process/Process_LogMessage/lane/Lane_Actorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Adjudicatorglossary-ledger.json | Settles a criterion whose reviewer entries disagree, and records WHY. Inherits reviewer because an adjudicator is a reviewer with one added entitlement — the adjudication permission — and the separation is the point: a reviewer reports, an adjudicator settles, and a process where every reviewer could settle has no way to say who decided. The KNOWLEDGE spreads (several roles carry the adjudication skill, because each has to tell an adjudicable disagreement from a complaint); the ENTITLEMENT does not, and lives on the actor as a permission.notation role/adjudicatorfirst seen 2026-09-22status current | . | Administratorglossary-ledger.json | Administers the role graph itself: who exists, what they may act as, and what they may do. The ONE lane whose activities change the substrate every other diagram's lanes bind to — which is why it is drawn rather than left as a filesystem edit. Declared 2026-09-20 on the owner's answer that administration is a swimlane; role-model.md's rule is that a role is never invented to make a diagram drawable, so it waited for that.notation role/administratorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Agentbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation process/Process_HumanAgentDiscussion/lane/Lane_Agentfirst seen 2026-10-01status current | . | Attestation serviceglossary-ledger.json | Signs a QA report's run hashes over an API. A MECHANICAL role, and the one that DISAPPEARS when the actor performing it cannot reach out — which is why the signing process carries a second, human lane rather than a retry.notation role/attestation-servicefirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Authorglossary-ledger.json | Writes and revises folio content. The position, not the person: an editor and a guideline developer both act as author when they are changing a block.notation role/authorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | The session agent doing the work. The broadest skill set here, and the one whose membership most needs auditing.notation role/authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Board rendererglossary-ledger.json | Draws a board and performs what the reader has already decided: reads each kind's declared zoom threshold and the layout layer, swaps a card for its avatar, projects an open window onto the canvas, and carries out a confirmed relocation. A system lane — it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, which is exactly why every decision in board-open-close.bpmn and board-relocate.bpmn sits in the reader's lane instead. It is NOT the build pipeline: it runs where the reader is, once per request, and publishes nothing.notation role/board-rendererfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Bootstrapping Agentbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation role/bootstrapping-agentfirst seen 2026-09-23status current | . | Build pipelineglossary-ledger.json | Validates, renders and publishes, and watches whether that actually worked. A system lane: it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, so anything needing a decision belongs in a different lane. It carries todo-manager for the two CI-watcher dispatch points in content-change-review, which claim and note a bean and never resolve one -- claim is idempotent and note appends, both fixed programs, while deciding that a publish SUCCEEDED is the judgement this lane must not make (bean xom7: docs-site.yml failed 30 times while reporting its own exit code).notation role/build-pipelinefirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Business analystglossary-ledger.json | Turns a stated need into a modelled requirement. Owns the CRDM lane and the BPMN/DMN that come out of it.notation role/business-analystfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Certifierglossary-ledger.json | Takes the certification decision on ONE test report: applies the DMN the plan's exitCriteria names (computed from facts, never asserted) and records the decision as a judgement under the declared attestations graph, from which it is signed through qa-report-signing.bpmn. A specialisation of stakeholder — accountable sign-off — but NOT judgementOnly: the exit criteria are a table it applies, and only the decision on top of them is the judgement (owner ruling, 2026-10-01). Never the tester and never the system under test. Bean 3o5b.notation role/certifierfirst seen 2026-10-01status current | . | Clinical / scientific SMEglossary-ledger.json | Reviewer whose judgement is about the subject matter rather than the artefact.notation role/clinical-smefirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Code reviewerglossary-ledger.json | Judges the knowledge graph's CODE nodes — Tool definitions in the tools graph and schema definition nodes under schemas/. Not ordinary code review: the question is whether the NODE is sound — does it declare what it is, do its references resolve, is the mechanism it advertises the one that runs — which a passing test suite does not answer. Entered by DESCENDING into Process_CodeReview.notation role/code-reviewerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Compute authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | Writes and audits the computation scripts and simulators that produce witnessed values, and keeps the paper's numbers and its computations from drifting apart.notation role/compute-authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Corpusglossary-ledger.json | The versioned content store and the L1 source knowledge graph. Like the work plan, a lane that is written to rather than a participant that acts.notation role/corpusfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Deep researcherglossary-ledger.json | Answers a question FROM a corpus already held, and is answerable for the answer. Distinct from librarian, which decides what to capture, and from ingestion-agent, which derives structure from what was captured: both produce the corpus, and this role consumes it. Added 2026-09-23 with the doc-researcher methodology, because the accountability it names — somebody who must stand behind a synthesis and its citations — belonged to no declared role. THE LANE IT BINDS IS DRAWN IN ANOTHER INSTANCE — the Deep researcher lane of folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn, which names this role with <folio:role ref>. It carried a lanes[] here for about an hour on 2026-09-23 before #1168 landed and inverted the relation: a lane names its role, and a role does not list its lanes, because a general node never names its users. The binding is therefore stated once, on the lane, and this role says nothing about where it is drawn.notation role/deep-researcherfirst seen 2026-09-23status current | . | Docs authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | The authoring agent producing what a person reads ABOUT the instance — generated references, the glossary, sticky notes, theme art and deployment documentation.notation role/docs-authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Editorglossary-ledger.json | Author plus the authority to accept a change into the corpus. The lane that sees QA findings and decides.notation role/editorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Editorial authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | The authoring agent in the editorial lane: auditing a block's prose, structure and sourcing rather than writing new subject matter.notation role/editorial-authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Evidence agentglossary-ledger.json | Retrieves and appraises external evidence for a guideline claim.notation role/evidence-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | External registryglossary-ledger.json | Trusted registries and observatories outside this instance's control. Carries no skills because nothing here instructs it.notation role/external-registryfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Feedback providerglossary-ledger.json | Offers a finding on content or code — a script checker, a review agent, a reader, an SME. PLURAL by design: an adjudication is the judgement of one or more feedback providers' feedback, and the process draws the lane once for any number of them. Not an adjudicator: this role states what it found and on what evidence, and has no entitlement to settle the disagreement its finding creates.notation role/feedback-providerfirst seen 2026-09-22status current | . | FHIR modellerglossary-ledger.json | Authors the L3 profiles, extensions and examples an IG is built from.notation role/fhir-modellerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Human translatorglossary-ledger.json | Produces the target-language text. Distinct from the coordinator because accepting one's own translation is the gate this separation removes.notation role/translatorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | IG publisher + validatorglossary-ledger.json | The JVM services an IG build shells out to. External in behaviour, internal in configuration.notation role/ig-publisher-servicefirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Ingestion engineglossary-ledger.json | Runs unattended over a source corpus. No user is in the room, so every gate it reaches must be decidable from the material.notation role/ingestion-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Initiatorbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | Retired 2026-09-23 — kept, never deleted, so retirement and accident do not look alike.notation role/initiatorfirst seen 2026-09-21status retired | . | Integration watcherglossary-ledger.json | Watches the default branch and open branches for newly-landed work that an existing audit axis should be re-run over. Reports findings; does not author the fix.notation role/integration-watcherfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Knowledge Graph Data Storebootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation role/knowledge-graph-data-storefirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | L1 extraction reviewerglossary-ledger.json | Signs, or rejects, the exclusions an L1 extraction proposes: each normative-looking sentence of a WHO publication that the curation says is not a recommendation, an implementation practice or a remark. Until a person acting in this role signs an exclusion, its sentence stays unaccounted and coverage stays below 100 %. Owner ruling 3b, 2026-10-12: exclusions are signed by this named role, never by the agent that proposed them. Inherits the harness's generic reviewer; the ontologist/terminologist skills, methodologies and processes that will equip it are bean 4nfs.notation role/l1-extraction-reviewerfirst seen 2026-10-15status current | . | Lean authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | Writes and repairs the Lean 4 formalization — translating narrative mathematics into declarations, keeping the build green, and curating what is staged for upstream.notation role/lean-authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Lean toolchainglossary-ledger.json | Elaborates and checks the formal half of a paper folio. Answers only what Lean can answer.notation role/lean-toolchainfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Librarianglossary-ledger.json | Acquires a source and files it. Distinct from ingestion-agent, which DERIVES structure from a source already in hand: this role decides what to capture, how faithfully, and what must be recorded at the moment of capture because nobody can reconstruct it later.notation role/librarianfirst seen 2026-09-22status current | . | Loggerbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation role/loggerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Merge stewardglossary-ledger.json | Stewards writes to ONE watched ref -- a long-lived branch several processes write and something downstream consumes serially. The ref is a parameter of the LANE INSTANCE, not of this persona, so main, gh-pages and each cat/cat-harness/* store branch can each have a steward without a schema change; a ref qualifies when a declaring directory's storage (or source) names it, or it is main/gh-pages. On main that work is a merge train: composes it from the queue, attributes and ejects on red, lands at the tested SHA. On a route-keyed ref it is coalescing: batches the writes arriving in one window into a single write. Decides nothing the reprioritisation table or the owner has not -- placement is computed by merge-priority.dmn, and landing waits for the owner's release. Records decisions on queue entries and windows, never the host's facts.notation role/merge-stewardfirst seen 2026-10-02status current | . | Narrative reviewerglossary-ledger.json | Judges PROSE — register and voice, the editorial dependencies a reader needs, and translation. Entered by DESCENDING into Process_NarrativeReview: the actor keeps its outer review role and adds these skills along that call path, rather than every reviewer carrying them everywhere.notation role/narrative-reviewerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Onboarding agentglossary-ledger.json | The authoring agent acting before there is a folio: clarifying what the user means by "create a folio", scanning an existing repo, and scaffolding.notation role/onboarding-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Platform authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | The authoring agent working on how this instance PUBLISHES itself — the MCP projection, its contract, and the rendering endpoints.notation role/platform-authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Programme managerglossary-ledger.json | Owns what gets worked on and holds release authority. The lane that authorises, and the one step no policy may relax.notation role/programme-managerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Proof review agentglossary-ledger.json | Reviews proofs — narrative and formal — for gaps, vacuity, redundancy and divergence between the two renderings of the same claim.notation role/proof-review-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Publication managerglossary-ledger.json | Takes an authorised release to its published form and is accountable for what is live.notation role/publication-managerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Publish targetglossary-ledger.json | GitHub Pages, or wherever the folio is served from. Reached, probed and reported on — never assumed live.notation role/publish-targetfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | QC reviewerglossary-ledger.json | Reviewer with the publication quality gate. Checks the built artefact, not only the source.notation role/qc-reviewerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Requestorbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation role/requestorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Review coordinatorglossary-ledger.json | Organises a review without deciding it. Pulls tagged review comments in, splits a large change into slices by section, assigns each slice to a reviewer of the right role, and watches coverage until every changed block has a verdict or a reasoned waiver. Cannot accept or reject: that is the editor's lane, and the separation is the owner's ruling (2026-09-23, bean en2d). Not a reviewer: it does not inherit one, because assigning a slice is not reading it.notation role/review-coordinatorfirst seen 2026-09-23status current | . | Reviewer / SMEglossary-ledger.json | Reads a change and judges it. Cannot accept it — that is the editor's lane — and the separation is why review findings are advice rather than commits. The GENERIC review position: what kind of thing changed decides which subprocess it descends into (review-task.bpmn), and the actor takes on that inner lane's role for the call path only.notation role/reviewerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Session coordinatorglossary-ledger.json | The authoring agent managing the SESSION rather than the content: what this session intends, what is already in flight elsewhere, and what to pick up next.notation role/session-coordinatorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Session recordglossary-ledger.json | A session's context — who is acting, which instances are open, what it waits on. A MECHANICAL role and an actedUpon one: written to as the session moves and read by a sibling deciding whether a claim is live, and it decides nothing. Modelled on work-plan, corpus and log, the stores that are acted upon rather than acting. It carries session-context because the shape of what is written IS the discipline here — unlike work-plan, whose store has a CLI, this one is written by a machine that may be an LLM playing the part, so the schema is the contract.notation role/session-recordfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Sibling sessionglossary-ledger.json | Another agent or human working the same store. Present in bean-lifecycle precisely to mark what is NOT yours to close.notation role/sibling-sessionfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Stakeholderglossary-ledger.json | Signs off that a requirement is met. Carries no skills deliberately: sign-off is a judgement, not a procedure, and a skill here would suggest an agent could supply it.notation role/stakeholderfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Terminologistglossary-ledger.json | Owns coded concepts and value sets — the vocabulary a DAK is expressed in.notation role/terminologistfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Test requesterglossary-ledger.json | Asks for a system under test to be certified against a named test-plan/v1 (plan id and version). It may BE the system under test, or speak for it, and that is exactly why it carries no lane after the request: the requester never tests, checks or certifies, so the system never writes a verdict about itself (untainted-verification; the test-sut-not-self-judged criterion). Lane Lane_Requester in test-plan-execution.bpmn, bean 3o5b.notation role/test-requesterfirst seen 2026-10-01status current | . | Testerglossary-ledger.json | Runs a test-plan/v1 against a system under test: resolves the plan, binds its test data (fixed and reviewed, or generated from template + params + seed, per vm6m), executes every case or skips it with a reason, and writes the folio-test-run/v1 and the test-report/v1. UNTAINTED from the system under test — never the same actor — and it does not certify: the rollup it writes is what the certifier decides ON. Bean 3o5b.notation role/testerfirst seen 2026-10-01status current | . | Translation adjudicatorglossary-ledger.json | Adjudicator who settles a disagreement between machine and human translation. The first specialisation of adjudicator, and the only one that existed before the role did — its lane documentation in translation-workflow.bpmn is where "a reviewer reports, an adjudicator settles" was written down.notation role/translation-adjudicatorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Translation coordinatorglossary-ledger.json | Decides what is translated, into which languages, and when a translation is accepted.notation role/translation-coordinatorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Untainted checkerglossary-ledger.json | Re-executes a SAMPLE of a plan's cases from the plan and the data alone — never the tester's verdicts — and reports whether it agrees. It rules on nothing: agreement is a fact the certification table reads, not a verdict the checker writes (untainted-verification rule 3: one party doing both halves is not this check). Lane Lane_Checker in test-plan-execution.bpmn, bean 3o5b.notation role/untainted-checkerfirst seen 2026-10-01status current | . | Userglossary-ledger.json | The person the assistant is working for. States intent, answers the questions the agent cannot decide from the filesystem, and confirms anything irreversible.notation role/userfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Validation pipelineglossary-ledger.json | The mechanical half of the HCI validation gate. 449.title: Glossary
449.content: Derived: every term this instance's swimlanes define — the role's title and description, the lane names that bind it, and whether the term has been retired. This is an index, not the documentation. It says what exists and what each artefact declares about itself. What a process is for, when you would be in it, and what it is not, is authored beside it and reuses these entries rather than restating them — see the auto-docs skill. Filter this table | Artefact | What it declares about itself | . | Activity logglossary-ledger.json | The agent activity log. A MECHANICAL role and an actedUpon one: it is written to at task start and task end, and emptied by an actor — one entry, all of them, or on a periodic sweep — and it decides nothing. Modelled on work-plan and corpus, the two existing stores that are acted upon rather than acting. Its entries are held in the instance's unpublished store and never reach a published graph; the activity-log skill names the location, which is deliberately not repeated here because a role description IS published.notation role/logfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Actorbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation process/Process_LogMessage/lane/Lane_Actorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Adjudicatorglossary-ledger.json | Settles a criterion whose reviewer entries disagree, and records WHY. Inherits reviewer because an adjudicator is a reviewer with one added entitlement — the adjudication permission — and the separation is the point: a reviewer reports, an adjudicator settles, and a process where every reviewer could settle has no way to say who decided. The KNOWLEDGE spreads (several roles carry the adjudication skill, because each has to tell an adjudicable disagreement from a complaint); the ENTITLEMENT does not, and lives on the actor as a permission.notation role/adjudicatorfirst seen 2026-09-22status current | . | Administratorglossary-ledger.json | Administers the role graph itself: who exists, what they may act as, and what they may do. The ONE lane whose activities change the substrate every other diagram's lanes bind to — which is why it is drawn rather than left as a filesystem edit. Declared 2026-09-20 on the owner's answer that administration is a swimlane; role-model.md's rule is that a role is never invented to make a diagram drawable, so it waited for that.notation role/administratorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Agentbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation process/Process_HumanAgentDiscussion/lane/Lane_Agentfirst seen 2026-10-01status current | . | Attestation serviceglossary-ledger.json | Signs a QA report's run hashes over an API. A MECHANICAL role, and the one that DISAPPEARS when the actor performing it cannot reach out — which is why the signing process carries a second, human lane rather than a retry.notation role/attestation-servicefirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Authorglossary-ledger.json | Writes and revises folio content. The position, not the person: an editor and a guideline developer both act as author when they are changing a block.notation role/authorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | The session agent doing the work. The broadest skill set here, and the one whose membership most needs auditing.notation role/authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Board rendererglossary-ledger.json | Draws a board and performs what the reader has already decided: reads each kind's declared zoom threshold and the layout layer, swaps a card for its avatar, projects an open window onto the canvas, and carries out a confirmed relocation. A system lane — it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, which is exactly why every decision in board-open-close.bpmn and board-relocate.bpmn sits in the reader's lane instead. It is NOT the build pipeline: it runs where the reader is, once per request, and publishes nothing.notation role/board-rendererfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Bootstrapping Agentbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation role/bootstrapping-agentfirst seen 2026-09-23status current | . | Build pipelineglossary-ledger.json | Validates, renders and publishes, and watches whether that actually worked. A system lane: it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, so anything needing a decision belongs in a different lane. It carries todo-manager for the two CI-watcher dispatch points in content-change-review, which claim and note a bean and never resolve one -- claim is idempotent and note appends, both fixed programs, while deciding that a publish SUCCEEDED is the judgement this lane must not make (bean xom7: docs-site.yml failed 30 times while reporting its own exit code).notation role/build-pipelinefirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Business analystglossary-ledger.json | Turns a stated need into a modelled requirement. Owns the CRDM lane and the BPMN/DMN that come out of it.notation role/business-analystfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Certifierglossary-ledger.json | Takes the certification decision on ONE test report: applies the DMN the plan's exitCriteria names (computed from facts, never asserted) and records the decision as a judgement under the declared attestations graph, from which it is signed through qa-report-signing.bpmn. A specialisation of stakeholder — accountable sign-off — but NOT judgementOnly: the exit criteria are a table it applies, and only the decision on top of them is the judgement (owner ruling, 2026-10-01). Never the tester and never the system under test. Bean 3o5b.notation role/certifierfirst seen 2026-10-01status current | . | Clinical / scientific SMEglossary-ledger.json | Reviewer whose judgement is about the subject matter rather than the artefact.notation role/clinical-smefirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Code reviewerglossary-ledger.json | Judges the knowledge graph's CODE nodes — Tool definitions in the tools graph and schema definition nodes under schemas/. Not ordinary code review: the question is whether the NODE is sound — does it declare what it is, do its references resolve, is the mechanism it advertises the one that runs — which a passing test suite does not answer. Entered by DESCENDING into Process_CodeReview.notation role/code-reviewerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Compute authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | Writes and audits the computation scripts and simulators that produce witnessed values, and keeps the paper's numbers and its computations from drifting apart.notation role/compute-authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Corpusglossary-ledger.json | The versioned content store and the L1 source knowledge graph. Like the work plan, a lane that is written to rather than a participant that acts.notation role/corpusfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Deep researcherglossary-ledger.json | Answers a question FROM a corpus already held, and is answerable for the answer. Distinct from librarian, which decides what to capture, and from ingestion-agent, which derives structure from what was captured: both produce the corpus, and this role consumes it. Added 2026-09-23 with the doc-researcher methodology, because the accountability it names — somebody who must stand behind a synthesis and its citations — belonged to no declared role. THE LANE IT BINDS IS DRAWN IN ANOTHER INSTANCE — the Deep researcher lane of folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn, which names this role with <folio:role ref>. It carried a lanes[] here for about an hour on 2026-09-23 before #1168 landed and inverted the relation: a lane names its role, and a role does not list its lanes, because a general node never names its users. The binding is therefore stated once, on the lane, and this role says nothing about where it is drawn.notation role/deep-researcherfirst seen 2026-09-23status current | . | Docs authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | The authoring agent producing what a person reads ABOUT the instance — generated references, the glossary, sticky notes, theme art and deployment documentation.notation role/docs-authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Editorglossary-ledger.json | Author plus the authority to accept a change into the corpus. The lane that sees QA findings and decides.notation role/editorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Editorial authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | The authoring agent in the editorial lane: auditing a block's prose, structure and sourcing rather than writing new subject matter.notation role/editorial-authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Evidence agentglossary-ledger.json | Retrieves and appraises external evidence for a guideline claim.notation role/evidence-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | External registryglossary-ledger.json | Trusted registries and observatories outside this instance's control. Carries no skills because nothing here instructs it.notation role/external-registryfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Feedback providerglossary-ledger.json | Offers a finding on content or code — a script checker, a review agent, a reader, an SME. PLURAL by design: an adjudication is the judgement of one or more feedback providers' feedback, and the process draws the lane once for any number of them. Not an adjudicator: this role states what it found and on what evidence, and has no entitlement to settle the disagreement its finding creates.notation role/feedback-providerfirst seen 2026-09-22status current | . | FHIR modellerglossary-ledger.json | Authors the L3 profiles, extensions and examples an IG is built from.notation role/fhir-modellerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Human translatorglossary-ledger.json | Produces the target-language text. Distinct from the coordinator because accepting one's own translation is the gate this separation removes.notation role/translatorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | IG publisher + validatorglossary-ledger.json | The JVM services an IG build shells out to. External in behaviour, internal in configuration.notation role/ig-publisher-servicefirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Ingestion engineglossary-ledger.json | Runs unattended over a source corpus. No user is in the room, so every gate it reaches must be decidable from the material.notation role/ingestion-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Initiatorbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | Retired 2026-09-23 — kept, never deleted, so retirement and accident do not look alike.notation role/initiatorfirst seen 2026-09-21status retired | . | Integration watcherglossary-ledger.json | Watches the default branch and open branches for newly-landed work that an existing audit axis should be re-run over. Reports findings; does not author the fix.notation role/integration-watcherfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Knowledge Graph Data Storebootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation role/knowledge-graph-data-storefirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | L1 extraction reviewerglossary-ledger.json | Signs, or rejects, the exclusions an L1 extraction proposes: each normative-looking sentence of a WHO publication that the curation says is not a recommendation, an implementation practice or a remark. Until a person acting in this role signs an exclusion, its sentence stays unaccounted and coverage stays below 100 %. Owner ruling 3b, 2026-10-12: exclusions are signed by this named role, never by the agent that proposed them. Inherits the harness's generic reviewer; the ontologist/terminologist skills, methodologies and processes that will equip it are bean 4nfs.notation role/l1-extraction-reviewerfirst seen 2026-10-15status current | . | Lean authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | Writes and repairs the Lean 4 formalization — translating narrative mathematics into declarations, keeping the build green, and curating what is staged for upstream.notation role/lean-authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Lean toolchainglossary-ledger.json | Elaborates and checks the formal half of a paper folio. Answers only what Lean can answer.notation role/lean-toolchainfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Librarianglossary-ledger.json | Acquires a source and files it. Distinct from ingestion-agent, which DERIVES structure from a source already in hand: this role decides what to capture, how faithfully, and what must be recorded at the moment of capture because nobody can reconstruct it later.notation role/librarianfirst seen 2026-09-22status current | . | Loggerbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation role/loggerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Merge stewardglossary-ledger.json | Stewards writes to ONE watched ref -- a long-lived branch several processes write and something downstream consumes serially. The ref is a parameter of the LANE INSTANCE, not of this persona, so main, gh-pages and each cat/cat-harness/* store branch can each have a steward without a schema change; a ref qualifies when a declaring directory's storage (or source) names it, or it is main/gh-pages. On main that work is a merge train: composes it from the queue, attributes and ejects on red, lands at the tested SHA. On a route-keyed ref it is coalescing: batches the writes arriving in one window into a single write. Decides nothing the reprioritisation table or the owner has not -- placement is computed by merge-priority.dmn, and landing waits for the owner's release. Records decisions on queue entries and windows, never the host's facts.notation role/merge-stewardfirst seen 2026-10-02status current | . | Narrative reviewerglossary-ledger.json | Judges PROSE — register and voice, the editorial dependencies a reader needs, and translation. Entered by DESCENDING into Process_NarrativeReview: the actor keeps its outer review role and adds these skills along that call path, rather than every reviewer carrying them everywhere.notation role/narrative-reviewerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Onboarding agentglossary-ledger.json | The authoring agent acting before there is a folio: clarifying what the user means by "create a folio", scanning an existing repo, and scaffolding.notation role/onboarding-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Platform authoring agentglossary-ledger.json | The authoring agent working on how this instance PUBLISHES itself — the MCP projection, its contract, and the rendering endpoints.notation role/platform-authoring-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Programme managerglossary-ledger.json | Owns what gets worked on and holds release authority. The lane that authorises, and the one step no policy may relax.notation role/programme-managerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Proof review agentglossary-ledger.json | Reviews proofs — narrative and formal — for gaps, vacuity, redundancy and divergence between the two renderings of the same claim.notation role/proof-review-agentfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Publication managerglossary-ledger.json | Takes an authorised release to its published form and is accountable for what is live.notation role/publication-managerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Publish targetglossary-ledger.json | GitHub Pages, or wherever the folio is served from. Reached, probed and reported on — never assumed live.notation role/publish-targetfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | QC reviewerglossary-ledger.json | Reviewer with the publication quality gate. Checks the built artefact, not only the source.notation role/qc-reviewerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Requestorbootstrap/glossary-ledger.json | no description in the artefactnotation role/requestorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Review coordinatorglossary-ledger.json | Organises a review without deciding it. Pulls tagged review comments in, splits a large change into slices by section, assigns each slice to a reviewer of the right role, and watches coverage until every changed block has a verdict or a reasoned waiver. Cannot accept or reject: that is the editor's lane, and the separation is the owner's ruling (2026-09-23, bean en2d). Not a reviewer: it does not inherit one, because assigning a slice is not reading it.notation role/review-coordinatorfirst seen 2026-09-23status current | . | Reviewer / SMEglossary-ledger.json | Reads a change and judges it. Cannot accept it — that is the editor's lane — and the separation is why review findings are advice rather than commits. The GENERIC review position: what kind of thing changed decides which subprocess it descends into (review-task.bpmn), and the actor takes on that inner lane's role for the call path only.notation role/reviewerfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Session coordinatorglossary-ledger.json | The authoring agent managing the SESSION rather than the content: what this session intends, what is already in flight elsewhere, and what to pick up next.notation role/session-coordinatorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Session recordglossary-ledger.json | A session's context — who is acting, which instances are open, what it waits on. A MECHANICAL role and an actedUpon one: written to as the session moves and read by a sibling deciding whether a claim is live, and it decides nothing. Modelled on work-plan, corpus and log, the stores that are acted upon rather than acting. It carries session-context because the shape of what is written IS the discipline here — unlike work-plan, whose store has a CLI, this one is written by a machine that may be an LLM playing the part, so the schema is the contract.notation role/session-recordfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Sibling sessionglossary-ledger.json | Another agent or human working the same store. Present in bean-lifecycle precisely to mark what is NOT yours to close.notation role/sibling-sessionfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Stakeholderglossary-ledger.json | Signs off that a requirement is met. Carries no skills deliberately: sign-off is a judgement, not a procedure, and a skill here would suggest an agent could supply it.notation role/stakeholderfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Terminologistglossary-ledger.json | Owns coded concepts and value sets — the vocabulary a DAK is expressed in.notation role/terminologistfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Test requesterglossary-ledger.json | Asks for a system under test to be certified against a named test-plan/v1 (plan id and version). It may BE the system under test, or speak for it, and that is exactly why it carries no lane after the request: the requester never tests, checks or certifies, so the system never writes a verdict about itself (untainted-verification; the test-sut-not-self-judged criterion). Lane Lane_Requester in test-plan-execution.bpmn, bean 3o5b.notation role/test-requesterfirst seen 2026-10-01status current | . | Testerglossary-ledger.json | Runs a test-plan/v1 against a system under test: resolves the plan, binds its test data (fixed and reviewed, or generated from template + params + seed, per vm6m), executes every case or skips it with a reason, and writes the folio-test-run/v1 and the test-report/v1. UNTAINTED from the system under test — never the same actor — and it does not certify: the rollup it writes is what the certifier decides ON. Bean 3o5b.notation role/testerfirst seen 2026-10-01status current | . | Translation adjudicatorglossary-ledger.json | Adjudicator who settles a disagreement between machine and human translation. The first specialisation of adjudicator, and the only one that existed before the role did — its lane documentation in translation-workflow.bpmn is where "a reviewer reports, an adjudicator settles" was written down.notation role/translation-adjudicatorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Translation coordinatorglossary-ledger.json | Decides what is translated, into which languages, and when a translation is accepted.notation role/translation-coordinatorfirst seen 2026-09-21status current | . | Untainted checkerglossary-ledger.json | Re-executes a SAMPLE of a plan's cases from the plan and the data alone — never the tester's verdicts — and reports whether it agrees. It rules on nothing: agreement is a fact the certification table reads, not a verdict the checker writes (untainted-verification rule 3: one party doing both halves is not this check). A low edge count over an unclassified corpus is the same false comfort as a green check over an empty one — and this rule is FIRST so no cross-edge count can outrank it. | . | Stands alone?cat-harness/processes/kg/decisions/isolation-gate.dmn | No declaration of its own: the directory moves and nothing downstream can resolve it. | . | Ready to seed?cat-harness/processes/kg/decisions/seed-readiness-gate.dmn | A PR marked as moving much of the tree is still open over this layer: the seed would snapshot one side of it. | . | Declared in place?cat-harness/processes/kg/decisions/subgraph-declared-gate.dmn | Could not determine. 562.title: Already somebody else’s concept? (не переведено)
562.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers. (не переведено) . The table’s labels are in the source language: it reports counts per scheme, computed by the gate rather than authored here. (не переведено) . Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 3748 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 3748 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin.
